raw_response:
I’m 64 now, and after 40 years on this land I don’t like making big changes unless I have a strong reason. I only finished middle school, so I listen to what the extension people say, but in the end I still go by what I’ve seen in my own fields and what the better farmers nearby are doing. I have 19.1 mu total, and with some family members working off-farm, I can’t spread myself too thin. So this year I’ll keep the main pattern steady: most of the land stays in wheat-maize double cropping, and a smaller piece stays in cotton. Wheat and maize are still the safer income for me, but cotton gives me another leg to stand on if grain price is weak.

For the land arrangement, I’ll put 12.1 mu into the wheat-maize rotation and 7.0 mu into cotton. The wheat on that 12.1 mu was planted in October 2025 and I’ll carry it through to harvest in June 2026, then turn that same land around fast into summer maize. For wheat, I won’t cut fertilizer too much because if wheat loses tillers, it’s hard to make up later. I’ll do a base fertilizer plus one topdress around jointing, and use well irrigation about 3 times if the spring stays dry. For maize, the turnaround after wheat is tight, so I’ll keep tillage simple, usually rotary till or even direct seeding after clearing straw if I can get the machine in time. Maize gets less water than wheat, maybe 1 time if rain is normal, 2 if it turns dry. Cotton I’ll manage more carefully but on fewer mu, because it takes more watching and picking. I’ll use a moderate fertilizer rate, not the highest, because cotton can eat money fast and labor is not as easy for my household now. My thinking is simple: steady wheat, quick maize, and limited cotton so I can still handle the work and not overspend early in the season.
